newsitem.title: USA: Genetic ID marketing test for altered crops.
newsitem.headline: Genetic ID marketing test for altered crops.

text.p: Genetic ID has developed a test to detect genetically-altered corn and soybeans that it is marketing in several countries, a company official said.
Privately-held Genetic ID provides genetic testing services.

The test, which scans corn and soybeans for altered DNA, is presently being marketed in the United States and Canada, as well as to European food producers concerned about genetically-altered products, said Genetic ID general manager, Jeffrey Wells.

In March 1996, the European Union gave a green light to imports of genetically-modified soybeans from the United States. But several EU member states opposed the majority decision by an EU regulatory committee on health and safety grounds.
"This test does test right at the genetic level and it positively detects whether the crop has been genetically altered or not," Wells said.
